questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Write a notice for your school notice board, in about 100 words, telling pet owners how to keep a dog or a cat healthy — how much to feed it, what to cut out, and how much exercise to give it.

markingPoints.description: Content: the notice explains that over-feeding and too little exercise weaken a pet and can make it ill.
Format: it has a clear heading, short numbered or bulleted points, and is signed by the issuer.
Organisation: the points move logically from the mistake to the rules the owner should follow.
Accuracy: correct subject-verb agreement, correct use of articles and correct spelling throughout.
Expression: simple, direct sentences and suitable imperatives, laid out for a notice board.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Pets Need Less Food and More Exercise

Many owners feed their pets rich extras whenever the animal begs. This is a mistake. A dog or cat that is over-fed and seldom exercised grows weak and listless and may fall ill. So please follow these simple rules: give your pet only its usual meals, cut down on sweets, and take it out for a walk every day. Say no kindly but firmly when your pet begs for more. A healthy pet needs discipline, not extra food.

The School Animal Care Club

evidence: You must harden your heart and keep him on a very strict diet.
If you don’t cut his food right down and give him more exercise he is going to be really ill.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: You are a veterinary surgeon. A client whose dog has grown fat, listless and unwilling to walk has been giving it rich extras between meals. Write a formal letter to the client, in about 100 words, telling her what must be changed.

markingPoints.description: Content: the letter states that the dog is over-fed rather than under-fed, and that the rich extras caused the illness.
Format: it follows the formal letter layout — salutation, body, closing and signature with the writer's designation.
Organisation: the advice comes in a clear order — diet first, then exercise, then firmness.
Accuracy: correct subject-verb agreement, articles, prepositions and spelling throughout.
Expression: a polite but firm tone, with clear instructions and no unnecessary wordiness.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Dear Mrs Pumphrey,

I have examined your dog and I am afraid his illness is not caused by a lack of food. He is fed far too well and seldom taken out. For the next fortnight please serve only his usual meal, cut out all cream cakes and chocolates, and give nothing sweet between meals. Take him out for a proper walk every day. Be firm even when he begs. If he seems weak, do not give him malt or cod-liver oil to build him up; that is exactly what has made him ill.

Yours sincerely,
Mr Herriot
Veterinary Surgeon

evidence: I thought he must be suffering from malnutrition, so I have been giving him some little extras between meals to build him up
Are you giving him plenty of exercise?

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Write a short article, in about 100 words, for your school magazine on why pets need daily exercise as much as proper food.

markingPoints.description: Content: the article explains that over-feeding with little exercise leaves a pet sluggish and weak.
Format: it has an attractive headline, a short body and a closing line that sums up the writer's view.
Organisation: the ideas move from the problem, to its effect, to what owners should do.
Accuracy: correct subject-verb agreement, comparatives and correct spelling throughout.
Expression: lively, simple language with at least one figure of speech, suitable for a magazine.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Why Pets Need Daily Exercise

Every pet owner wants a healthy animal, yet many of us give our dogs and cats plenty of food and almost no exercise. A pet that is over-fed and rarely exercised becomes sluggish and lazy, exactly like a child who is given too many sweets and no games. Daily walks and outdoor play keep a pet's body healthy, its spirits high and its appetite regular. So walk your dog every day, let it run about in the park, and keep biscuits for rewards and not for meals. Exercise is a duty, not a luxury.

evidence: he has his little walks with me as you can see, but Hodgkin, the gardener, has been down with lumbago, so there has been no ring-throwing lately.
You must harden your heart and keep him on a very strict diet.

markingPoints.description: She noticed that Tricki was listless and seemed to have no energy.

questions.stem: Why did Tricki recover so quickly after he was taken into the surgery?

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Trace, in order, the steps by which the veterinary surgeon's treatment changed Tricki's condition, giving the steps in the correct sequence.

markingPoints.description: He was put on a strict diet, yet refused even his favourite dishes, vomited and lay panting.
The surgeon took him out of the house to the surgery to be kept under observation for about a fortnight.
For two days he was given no food at all but plenty of water in a warm loose box.
On the third day he began to whimper when he heard the dogs in the yard.
He joined the dogs, ate with the pack, scrimmaged and hunted rats, and needed no medicinal treatment.
In two weeks he was transformed into a lithe, hard-muscled animal keeping up with the pack.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. Tricki was put on a strict diet, but within a few days he refused even his favourite dishes, vomited and lay panting on a rug.
2. The surgeon took him out of the house to the surgery, to be kept under observation for about a fortnight.
3. For two days he got no food but plenty of water in a warm loose box; on the third day he began to whimper at the sound of the dogs in the yard.
4. He was then let out to join the dogs. He ate with the pack, scrimmaged with them and hunted rats in the old hen-house, needing no medicinal treatment.
5. In two weeks he was transformed into a lithe, hard-muscled animal keeping up with the pack.

evidence: The expected call came within a few days. Mrs Pumphrey was distraught. Tricki would eat nothing.
For two days I kept an eye on him, giving him no food but plenty of water.
In two weeks he had been transformed into a lithe, hard-muscled animal

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: A reader finds the remark “This is a triumph of surgery!” a surprising one to hear. Give the chain of reasons, in steps, that makes the remark apt.

markingPoints.description: No operation is performed and no medicinal treatment of any kind is given.
Tricki's illness was caused by his over-feeding, not by any lack of food.
Mrs Pumphrey fed him malt, cod-liver oil, Horlicks, cream cakes and chocolates, and could not cut the sweets.
He got little exercise, since there had been no ring-throwing because Hodgkin had lumbago.
The surgeon took him out of the house for about a fortnight, gave no food for two days but plenty of water, and let him live with the dogs.
He ate with the pack, scrimmaged and hunted rats, and in two weeks became lithe and hard-muscled, so the cure was exercise and company.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. No operation is performed and no medicinal treatment of any kind is given.
2. Tricki's illness was caused by his own mistress, who thought him malnourished and fed him malt, cod-liver oil, Horlicks, cream cakes and chocolates.
3. She could not cut down the sweets, and there was no ring-throwing because Hodgkin had lumbago.
4. He then refused even his favourite dishes, had bouts of vomiting and lay panting on a rug.
5. The surgeon got him out of the house for about a fortnight, gave him no food for two days but plenty of water, and let him live with the dogs.
6. He ate with the pack, scrimmaged and hunted rats, and in two weeks became lithe and hard-muscled. The cure was exercise and company, not surgery.

evidence: He had no medicinal treatment of any kind
He does love cream cakes and chocolates so. I can’t bear to refuse him.
Tricki’s only fault was greed.
